subject: LinqTech demo — model shortlist & action plan
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Matthew Kaplan <matthew.kaplan@linqtech.com>, Sara Bruner <sara.bruner@linqtech.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: LinqTech demo — model shortlist & action plan

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really appreciated the context on your customer support use case and the 95th-percentile latency sensitivity. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side.

Summary of needs you called out:
- ~120 concurrent agents (peak), ~25 req/s sustained for chat endpoint
- Tight latency target: p95 < 350ms for 2–4 turns (~80 tokens per response)
- Low tolerance for factual hallucination on policy/legal answers
- Data residency preference: US-only logging, with SLA for retention and audit export

Model shortlist (recommended for POC) and rationale:
1) redwood-neo-3.7b-q4 (recommended starter)
   - Tradeoff: best per-token cost and CPU/GPU memory profile; p95 latency comfortably under 200ms on our Dedicated M60 stacks for 80-token responses.
   - Quality: strong instruction-following; recommend adding our safety tuning layer for policy answers.
2) gptx-lite-13b-8bit
   - Tradeoff: ~2x cost vs 3.7b but noticeably higher precision on long-context QA and fewer hallucinations in our benchmarks. p95 ~320ms on Dedicated A40 pools with batching.
3) openmix-70b-quant-a (fallback for highest accuracy)
   - Tradeoff: highest quality but >3x cost; p95 latency ~550ms unless we provision more capacity and use 4-shard serving. Use as fallback for escalation flows only.

Benchmarks and assets I attached/linked:
- latency/throughput CSV: model-latency-benchmarks.csv (attached)
- prompt set we used for eval: linq_prompt_set_v2.jsonl (attached)
- demo recording: linqtech-demo-recording.mp4 (attached)
- live evaluation dashboard: https://app.redwood.com/evals/DEAL-7291/prompt-set-v2

Proposed next steps:
- Redwood provides a 2-week POC environment (dedicated tenant) with the 3 models above. We'll pre-load your prompt set and run automated quality regressions.
- You confirm procurement contact and any NDA requirements.
- We capture a short security questionnaire (SOC2 scoping) and a sample data flow for your infra team.

Can you confirm: (1) procurement contact email, (2) whether US-only logging satisfies your legal team, and (3) an initial throughput target we should pre-provision for the POC?

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

Connor — thanks for the thorough recap. Helpful. A couple quick clarifying Qs from our side:
- Can you share the exact prompt examples you used for the hallucination benchmarks? Our security lead will want to see the edge-case prompts.
- Ballpark pricing: can you give a cost/month estimate for steady-state 1M tokens/day (mix of gen+context) for the 3.7b vs 13b options?
- For the 70b fallback: is there a suggested canary strategy so we don't expose that model to all live traffic at once?

I'll loop in procurement once we have a rough cost and an initial SOW.

Matt
Chief Product Officer | Linq Tech
matthew.kaplan@linqtech.com
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 08:43:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: LinqTech demo — model shortlist & action plan

Connor — quick internal note before I reply to Matt:
- Swap recommendation: instead of openmix-70b as the primary fallback, propose we add openmix-34b-qat as an intermediate option. Gives most of the quality uplift at ~60% of the 70b cost and reduces latency pressure.
- Prepare: an eval run that includes our "safety/regression" hooks (prompt-set v3) — link below. That will catch policy drift for legal-related answers.
- Canary idea: start with 2% of production traffic to openmix-34b-qat with automatic rollback on the quality monitor (threshold = +5% hallucination rate vs baseline). Also ensure token-level cost telemetry is exported to their finance contact.

I'll reference our standardized canary config and the alert thresholds in the reply. Marissa, can you prepare the short canary JSON and the telemetry export snippet?

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Subject: Updated plan & quick pricing ballpark

Matt — following Vanessa's internal suggestion, updated shortlist and immediate plan below. Thanks for the quick questions — answers inline.

Updated shortlist for POC:
- redwood-neo-3.7b-q4 (primary: cost-efficient starter)
- gptx-lite-13b-8bit (primary: higher-quality tradeoff)
- openmix-34b-qat (fallback: quality-oriented but lower latency/cost than 70b)

Answers to your questions:
- Prompt examples: attached (linq_prompt_set_v2.jsonl) and we'll also run v3 for safety checks: https://app.redwood.com/evals/DEAL-7291/prompt-set-v3
- Pricing (ballpark, monthly for ~1M tokens/day sustained):
   * redwood-neo-3.7b-q4: ~$3,200 / month
   * gptx-lite-13b-8bit: ~$6,800 / month
   * openmix-34b-qat: ~$14,500 / month (used only for escalations/canary)
  These include token usage and baseline dedicated capacity amortization for p95 targets; exact numbers require commitment/region.
- Canary: Vanessa recommends starting at 2% traffic to openmix-34b-qat with our automatic rollback and quality alerting. We will provide the canary JSON and the telemetry exporter snippet.

Next steps we propose (action items):
- Connor: provision POC tenant and seed with prompt-set v2; start automated evals (ETA 48 hours).
- Vanessa/Marissa: prepare canary config + telemetry export (ETA 24 hours).
- Matt: share procurement contact and confirm US-only logging OK for legal team (or flag further constraints).

If procurement is ready we can attach a short SOW and start the POC within one business day of the NDA/SOW sign.
